info.name: EffectCraft integration
info.summary: Make motion graphics and effects in Nextcloud with EffectCraft
info.description:
Open an EffectCraft project or a video (MP4, MOV, WebM) in Files with **Edit in EffectCraft** and work right in the browser, the way you know from After Effects: compositions, layers, keyframes, hundreds of effects, layer styles, expressions, 3D cameras and lights, and the Render Queue.
- A video is imported as footage. **Save** stores the project (.ecproj) in the folder you pick the first time, and to that file from then on. - Opening a saved project fetches its footage from your Nextcloud. - Render Queue outputs store the file in any folder you pick. - If someone else changes the project while you have it open, you choose whether to replace their version or save a copy. - Optionally, clicking an EffectCraft project in Files opens it in EffectCraft.
EffectCraft runs entirely in your browser as WebAssembly. Files go only between your browser and your Nextcloud, and the server needs no extra software.
This is a community integration based on [EffectCraft](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft) by the ArtCraft team, an open-source, Rust-native motion graphics and visual effects app. It embeds a build of EffectCraft and is not made or endorsed by the ArtCraft team.
**Requirements:** a browser with WebGPU or WebGL2, and a web server that serves `.wasm` files as `application/wasm` (Nextcloud's own Apache and nginx configurations do).
info.author: Britton Couchman
